catalog_quote: To remove any lingering misconceptions that the resemblances between Tai-Kadai and Austronesian are due to chance, I give below comparisons involving Buyang, a recently-described Tai-Kadai language from the Kra branch, spoken near the China-Vietnam border (data from Li Jinfang 1999). While TK languages generally reflect An disyllables as monosyllables (either by losing the first syllable, or by collapsing the two), Buyang is remarkable in that it preserves several An disyllables as disyllables (Table 6). Observe that in these words, the first syllable is reduced: the vowel is always /a/, the syllable is toneless ('tone zero'), and the inventory of initial consonants is limited to a few: m- (for An m- and w-), q- (for An q- and k-), t- (for An C- and t-). new_statements.rule_in_words: No opened source uses the word 'stress' for Langjia/Langnian Buyang. What is stated (Li 1999 via Sagart 2004 and Edmondson draft; Li 1999/2002/1998 snippets and abstracts in Chinese) is that the language is tonal (Langjia: six tones 33, 24, 31, 312, 54, 11) and that the prefix/presyllable of sesquisyllabic words is reduced, vowel a, and carries no tone (轻声 'neutral/light tone', tone 0; 33 in slow speech), so the full tone and prominence sit on the final major syllable. That is a tonelessness statement, not a stress rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Li & Luo 2010 (Paha, not Langjia): some prefixes vary between a phonemic tone and the neutral tone; Li 1998 abstract: prefixes read 33 in slow speech.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (sesquisyllabic lexical words: prefix + major syllable); statements are second-hand from Li 1999 (Langjia). The only first-hand text held by the project (Li & Luo 2010) is Paha Buyang, a different ISO language [yha].
new_statements.identity_note: Langnian Buyang [yln] = the Langjia 郎架 (郎念土语: Langjia + Nianlang villages, Gula township, Funing) variety of Eastern Buyang, the variety Li Jinfang 1999 布央语研究 describes in detail (Li 2003 abstract; Glottolog alt. names Langjia, Langjia Buyang). All open first-hand Buyang descriptions held by the project (Li & Luo 2010 PL 607, Li & Luo 2006 LTBA, Li 1996) are of Paha/Baha Buyang [yha] = baha1256, and Ostapirat 2000 uses Ecun = E'ma Buyang [yzg] = emab1235; the Sagart 2004 and Edmondson statements quoted here are explicitly from Li 1999 (Langjia) and carry Langjia tone values.
